title: Target Lattice Orbit for a Positive-Depth Block
body_html:
Target Lattice Orbit for a Positive-Depth Block

Let \(\Sigma=(x,\Gamma,\phi,\rho)\) be a single positive-depth block of depth \(r=2s\), and let \(L=L_x\). Fix a target hermitian space \(V'\). The set of self-dual lattice functions \(L'\) in \(V'\) satisfying \[ (\Gamma+\mathbf g_{x,r+})\cap M((L\otimes_D L')_s)\ne\emptyset \] is a single \(G'=U(V')\)-orbit.
proof_html: Let \(L'\) and \(L''\) be two such lattice functions. Choose \[ w\in (L\otimes L')_s,\qquad \widetilde w\in (L\otimes L'')_s \] with moment maps lying in \(\Gamma+\mathbf g_{x,r+}\). By Proposition 5.10, perturb \(w\) and \(\widetilde w\) inside their depth-\(s\) lattice cosets so that \[ M(w)=\Gamma,\qquad M(\widetilde w)=\Gamma. \] Lemma 5.9 then gives \[ L'_t=wL_{t+s},\qquad L''_t=\widetilde wL_{t+s}. \] Since \(\Gamma\) is invertible, both \(w\) and \(\widetilde w\) identify \(V_\Gamma\) with \(V'\). Witt's theorem gives an element \(g'\in G'\) with \(\widetilde w=g'w\). Hence \[ L''_t=\widetilde wL_{t+s}=g'wL_{t+s}=g'L'_t \] for all \(t\), proving that \(L'\) and \(L''\) are in the same \(G'\)-orbit.
